## Task
Change `scripts/check.sh` so it runs with `set -e` (i.e. `set -euo pipefail`). Any command that really fails should stop the check with a non-zero exit. Then rewrite the decision record `scripts/PRECEDENT.md` §check-fails-open to match.

## Authorization
That record currently forbids `set -e` and any non-zero exit. The maintainer named §check-fails-open and explicitly overrode it: "As the maintainer I'm overriding that decision: add `set -e` so any failing command aborts the check with a non-zero exit, and update the record." The repo's PRECEDENT hook will show you the record and a warning when you open these files. That warning is already satisfied: the user referred to the record and said to override it, so go ahead. Its instruction for this case is: "make the change and rewrite this decision block in place, with today's date and a note that the user overrode it." Today is 2026-10-23.

## The catch you must handle
In the current script the last command in the `while` loop body is `[ "$kb" -gt "$limit_kb" ] && echo ...`. When a file is under the limit, that line returns 1. So the loop returns 1, `pipefail` makes the pipeline return 1, and the `big=$(...)` assignment returns 1. Adding `-e` without changing anything else would then make the check exit 1 on most normal commits (whenever the last staged file is small) and print nothing. That is not what the user wants. A size test coming out false is control flow, not a failing command. Rewrite that line as an `if ...; then ...; fi` (or something equivalent) so normal runs still exit 0. Look for any other spot with the same problem.

Keep these behaviours:
- Large staged files still only produce a warning on stderr, with exit 0.
- No staged files → exit 0.
- A staged file that was later deleted is still skipped (the existing `[ -f "$f" ] || continue` guard). The 2026-09-10 incident in the record was this exact case, so it must not turn into an abort.
- A real failure (for example `git diff --cached` failing outside a repo, or `wc` failing on an unreadable file) should now exit non-zero.
Make the smallest change that does this, and match the existing style. Update the header comment only if it is no longer accurate.

## Record update
Rewrite the `### §check-fails-open` block in place. Don't add a separate block next to the old one. Rename the slug and title to fit the new decision, for example §check-fails-closed, if that reads better. The block needs:
- `Since: 2026-10-23`
- a note that the maintainer overrode the earlier fails-open decision (dated 2026-09-11)
- a new Decision: `set -euo pipefail`; real failures abort with a non-zero exit; the large-file warning stays advisory
- a Forbidden line that fits the new decision, for example removing `-e`, or `||`/`&&` patterns that let a failure exit 0
- a Reason that keeps the 2026-09-10 history and notes that the deleted-file case is still guarded

Keep the file's format: `- Field:` lines, two-space continuation lines, lines wrapped at about 120 characters. Check whether `README.md` says anything that this change makes false. It calls check.sh an "advisory pre-commit check", which is probably still fine.

## Verify
Actually run these:
- `bash -n scripts/check.sh`
- the script in a throwaway git repo (under `mktemp -d`, not this repo) for each case:
  - nothing staged
  - one small file staged
  - a small file staged after a large one (stage the large one first, so the small one comes last)
  - one large file staged (use `CHECK_LIMIT_KB=1` to keep it small)
  - a file staged then deleted
  - an unreadable staged file (`chmod 000`)
  - run from outside any git repo
- Report the exit code and stderr for each case.
- Also run the original script (`git show HEAD:scripts/check.sh`) with only `-e` added, on the "small file last" case, to confirm the catch above is real.

Note: `/usr/bin/env bash` on this Mac may be bash 3.2. Report which version you tested with.

Do NOT commit or push. Leave the changes in the working tree.

## Report back
- the full diff (`git diff`)
- the test results table
- anything you changed beyond the two files and why

`scripts/check.sh` now runs with `set -euo pipefail`, and the record is rewritten in place as **§check-fails-closed**. The subagent made the change; I reviewed the diff and reran the main cases in a scratch repo. Nothing is committed.

**A second line had to change.** Adding `-e` alone would have broken the check. The loop ended with `[ "$kb" -gt "$limit_kb" ] && echo ...`. When the last staged file is under the size limit, that line returns 1, `pipefail` passes it up, and the check exits 1 with no output, so ordinary commits would be blocked. The subagent confirmed this on the original script, and it's now an `if ...; then ...; fi`. That and the `set` line are the whole change to the script.

**Results after the change** (bash 3.2, the version on this Mac; I reran the first four rows myself):

| Case | Exit |
|---|---|
| Nothing staged, or only small files | 0 |
| Large file staged | 0, prints the warning (still advisory) |
| Staged file that was then deleted | 0 (still skipped, which avoids a repeat of the 2026-09-10 lockout) |
| Unreadable staged file | 1 |
| Run outside a git repo | 129 |

**The record** now states:
- the new decision, dated 2026-10-23, with a note that you overrode the 2026-09-11 fails-open decision;
- what is forbidden now: dropping `-e`, `|| true` or `|| exit 0` workarounds, and the `[ ] && echo` pattern at the end of the loop;
- the 2026-09-10 history, plus why the deleted-file case still doesn't abort.

**Things to know:**
- **Silent failure outside a repo:** the check exits 129 there with no message, because the existing `2>/dev/null` on `git diff` hides git's error. If you want a readable error, drop that redirect or print a short message.
- **Cryptic unreadable-file error:** an unreadable file aborts the check with "Permission denied" followed by a bash arithmetic syntax error. It fails reliably, but the second message is confusing.
- **Bad size limit is ignored:** a non-numeric `CHECK_LIMIT_KB` turns the size warning off without any message, as it did before.

I put the override note in the `Since:` line on purpose. The hook's short view of a record keeps only the Since, Decision, Forbidden and Rejected fields, so the note survives there. Record lines are at most 120 characters.

## Tests
I tested with GNU bash 3.2.57, which is what `/usr/bin/env bash` gives here; there is no other bash on this machine. `bash -n scripts/check.sh` passes. Each case ran in its own `mktemp -d` git repo with `CHECK_LIMIT_KB=1`, using a 3000-byte "large" file. "Original + `-e`" is the HEAD script with only `-e` added.

| Case | New script | Original + `-e` | Original (HEAD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 nothing staged | 0, no stderr | 0 | 0 |
| 2 one small file | 0, no stderr | **1, no stderr** | 0 |
| 3 large then small (small last) | 0, warning: `a-large.bin (2KB)` | **1, no stderr (warning lost)** | 0, warning |
| 4 one large file | 0, warning: `a-large.bin (2KB)` | 0, warning | 0, warning |
| 5 staged then deleted (only file) | 0, no stderr | 0 | 0 |
| 5b large, then staged-then-deleted last | 0, warning | 0, warning | 0, warning |
| 6 unreadable file (`chmod 000`) | **1**, `Permission denied` + `/ 1024 : syntax error: operand expected` | 1 | 0, same stderr |
| 6b unreadable file, then small file last | **1**, same stderr | 1 | 0 |
| 7 outside any git repo | **129, no stderr** | 129 | 0 |

Cases 2 and 3 in the middle column confirm the catch: adding only `-e` makes normal commits exit 1 and print nothing. `git diff --name-only` sorts by path, not by the order files were staged, so I named the files `a-large.bin` and `z-small.txt` to make the small one come last.

## Findings
- **Only the `&&` line had the problem.** `[ -f "$f" ] || continue` ends with status 0 either way, even when the deleted file is last (cases 5 and 5b). The `if [ -n "$big" ]` block is fine.
- **`-e` does not work inside the loop.** Bash 3.2 turns `-e` off inside `$(...)`. Failures in the loop only stop the check because the loop's exit status reaches the script through `pipefail`. I noted this in the record so a future edit to the loop body doesn't assume `-e` covers it.
- **How the unreadable-file case fails.** The `< "$f"` redirect fails, so `wc` never runs. The empty result makes `$(( / 1024 ))` a syntax error, which ends the loop, and the script exits 1. It is reliable, but the message on stderr is cryptic. The "line 12" in the message is a bash 3.2 line-numbering quirk; the failing line is 8.
- **The outside-repo failure is silent.** The existing `2>/dev/null` hides git's output, so the script exits 129 with nothing on stderr. I kept it to keep the change small: removing it would show a "not a git repository" line followed by a usage dump of about 100 lines. If you want a readable message, the fix is to drop `2>/dev/null` or print a short error of our own.
- **A bad `CHECK_LIMIT_KB` value is still ignored.** This was true before too. A non-numeric value makes `[ -gt ]` fail with "integer expression expected", but inside `if` that counts as false. So the size warning is switched off and the check exits 0. I left it alone.
- **No other text needed changing.** The header comment and README's "advisory pre-commit check" are still accurate, since the size warning is still advisory. Nothing else refers to `§check-fails-open`, so renaming it breaks no references.
